Q: Weird `std::variant::operator==` error with clang + libc++ and specific number of variants A:

It works with -stdlib=libstdc++

It confirms a known category of issues where libc++'s internal implementation of std::variant (specifically the visitation and comparison logic) is not as "recursion-friendly" as libstdc++ (GNU's version)

If you wantr you can report it.

Q: Why does TypeScript not issue an error on a missing semicolon at the end of a statement? A:

Typescript, as a superset of JS, utilises the latter's Automatic Semicolon Insertion. If you want to learn more about where it will be implicitly put, read here -> http://inimino.org/~inimino/blog/javascript_semicolons .

Q: How can I disable automatic semicolon for auto imports with TypeScript and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code? A:

VS Code 1.38 tries to infer if semicolons should be used for auto imports and refactoring in JavaScript and TypeScript.

With VS Code 1.39 and TypeScript 3.7+, you can also explicitly set if semicolons should be used or not:

"javascript.format.semicolons": "remove",
"typescript.format.semicolons": "remove"

(Note that until VS Code 1.40 is released, you may need to install this extension in order to actually enable TypeScript 3.7 in VS Code)

Q: Tasks.json - detecting a Windows errorlevel return value from a shell task? A:

Thanks, but not sure I follow. In the above example I just want to know if FOO.exe returned a non-zero errorlevel. If it did, I would consider the task failed, otherwise the task is successful if the errorlevel is zero.

The equivalent check in a batch file (BAT, CMD) would be: if not errorlevel 1 goto success

Or, are you implying that unless another task depends on this one, it doesn't matter if we check the return code? It would be up to the developer to visually see if there was an error message.

Q: Why are there so few open-source C libraries for extracting embedded images from older Excel .xls files? A:

If you have many files, it is often easier to convert them to .xlsx first (using unoconv or Excel itself). Once they are .xlsx, you can extract images simply by unzipping the file:

unzip your_file.xlsx -d temp_folder
# Look in temp_folder/xl/media/
